title: Ministry of Corporate Affairs hosts the PMIS Industry Awards in New Delhi to honour leading partner companies for  creating meaningful internship opportunities for youth under the Prime Minister Internship Scheme
subtitle: PMIS interns also to participate in the Independence Day celebrations in New Delhi
body_text:
As part of the Independence Day celebrations, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA), Government of India, organized the PMIS Industry Awards on August 14, 2026, in New Delhi to recognize the contribution of partner companies in the successful implementation of the Prime Minister Internship Scheme (PMIS) during its pilot phase.
The event was chaired by the Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, and was attended by senior officials of the Ministry, representatives from leading industry partners, and more than 100 current and former PMIS interns from across the country.
The awards celebrated organizations that have demonstrated exceptional commitment to nurturing young talent, creating high-quality internship opportunities, adopting effective internship management practices, and supporting the Government’s vision of building a future-ready workforce. Mahindra & Mahindra Limited was recognized as the Overall Industry Champion for its leadership and exemplary contribution to promoting internships and youth engagement under PMIS.
Industry representatives shared positive experiences from their participation in the Scheme and highlighted the value created for both organizations and interns. A representative from Mahindra & Mahindra Limited said, “Today, we have crossed the milestone of welcoming 1,000 interns across the Mahindra Group.
This is nearly five times the number of interns who joined us in Round II and reflects how the PM Internship Scheme has evolved from a budding initiative into a programme operating at scale.” IBM also highlighted the value that interns bring to companies, noting that their fresh perspectives, curiosity, and willingness to learn have enriched teams, supported innovation, and reinforced the importance of developing future-ready, industry-relevant skills.
A representative from Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories shared an inspiring example of how PMIS is helping interns build future pathways, recalling that an intern used the PMIS internship certificate to secure admission to a pharmaceutical course at Long Island University, Brooklyn. The example reflected the Scheme’s potential not only to provide workplace exposure but also to support higher education and long-term career growth.
Western Coalfields Limited expressed appreciation for the Scheme, noting that PMIS helped the organization attract young talent to collieries in rural and semi-urban areas of Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, where sourcing interns had traditionally been challenging. The experience demonstrated the Scheme’s ability to connect youth with opportunities beyond major urban centres while addressing manpower requirements across diverse industry locations .
Award Category Winner(s) Overall Industry Champion Mahindra & Mahindra Limited Top PSU Partners Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) NTPC Limited Western Coalfields Limited Top Private Partners Reliance Industries Limited Infosys Limited Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Limited Pre-Internship Excellence Award HDFC Bank Limited Internship Management Excellence Award Shriram Finance Limited Innovation in Program Implementation Award IBM India Private Limited Innovation in Exit Pathways Award Power Grid Corporation of India Limited
In addition to the main award categories, organizations were recognized as Sectoral Champions for their outstanding performance and contribution within their respective industries under the Prime Minister Internship Scheme.
Sector Champion Organization(s) Metals & Mining Central Coalfields Limited FMCG ITC Limited Agriculture & Allied DCM Shriram Limited Healthcare Dr. Lal PathLabs Limited Pharmaceutical Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Limited Emcure Pharmaceuticals Limited Banking & Financial Services National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. Oil, Gas & Energy Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited Oil India Limited IT & Software Development Tech Mahindra Limited Infrastructure & Construction Larsen & Toubro Limited Automotive Mahindra & Mahindra Limited Diversified Conglomerates Reliance Industries Limited Retail & Consumer Durables Tata Consumer Products Limited
The Prime Minister Internship Scheme (PMIS) is aimed at providing youth with paid internship opportunities in top companies of India to enhance the employability of youth. Under PMIS, internship opportunities are available in multiple sectors across India for skilling, reskilling and upskilling the youth through practical workplace exposure, industry experience, and structured engagement with top companies.

enrichment.summary: On 14 August 2026, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs held the PMIS Industry Awards in New Delhi to recognize companies that excelled in implementing the Prime Minister Internship Scheme (PMIS) during its pilot phase. Mahindra & Mahindra was named Overall Industry Champion, with PSUs like ONGC, NTPC and Western Coalfields, and private firms like Reliance, Infosys and Dr. Reddy's also honoured across categories including Pre-Internship Excellence, Internship Management Excellence, and sectoral champion awards. The event, attended by over 100 current and former interns, was part of Independence Day celebrations.
enrichment.context: The Prime Minister Internship Scheme (PMIS) was launched to give youth paid internship exposure in India's top companies as part of the government's employability and skilling agenda, forming part of the broader 2024 Budget package on employment and skilling. The scheme connects the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (which administers CSR and corporate governance) with industry to place young interns, including in PSUs and rural/semi-urban locations, addressing both youth unemployment and talent-sourcing challenges for companies. This release is essentially a ceremonial recognition event for the scheme's pilot-phase partners rather than a new policy announcement, though it does surface some implementation data (e.g., Mahindra crossing 1,000 interns) that illustrates the scheme's scale-up from earlier rounds.
